captions.caption: Two men are at a campsite in a wooded area near a lake, with one man tending to a fire where a bird is roasting.
The camera captures a wide shot of the woods with the two men and their campfire in the background.
A man uses a tool to hammer something into the ground in the middle of a dense, leafless forest.
A close-up view shows a person's hands sharpening a small knife against a leather strop.
The person continues to run the blade of the knife back and forth along the leather strop to hone the edge.
The hands repeatedly flip the knife over and stroke it against the sharpening strop in a rhythmic motion.
The focus remains on the hands and the sharpening tool as the knife blade is being meticulously refined.
A wooden cup filled with a steaming liquid sits on a canvas bag next to some wooden weaving tools.
Steam rises from the hot beverage in the rustic wooden cup placed outdoors on a rucksack.
In the background, a man is out of focus while a bird roasts over a campfire next to a hanging kettle.
The bird continues to roast on a wooden spit over the open flames, with a black kettle hanging nearby.
A man's hands use a sharp knife to carefully carve and shape a flat piece of light-colored wood.
The woodworker shaves off thin curls of wood to refine the shape of the wooden object he is creating.
The man examines a wooden shuttle he is making, holding it against another piece of wood to check the fit.
Close-up of hands using a knife to carve a small hole or notch into a flat piece of wood.
The person uses the tip of the knife to meticulously remove small bits of wood from the surface of the workpiece.
The knife blade is used to scrape and smooth the edges of the hole being carved into the wood.
Fine wood shavings fall onto the person's trousers as they continue the detailed carving work.
The person uses the knife to carve out a rectangular section from the center of the wooden strip.
Hands carefully maneuver the knife to broaden the opening in the piece of wood being worked on.
The focus shifts to the man's hands as he carves more wood away, creating a specific shape for the tool.
Small curls of wood are peeled away by the sharp blade, revealing the inner texture of the timber.
The craftsman continues to refine the wooden piece, focusing on carving out a slot in the middle.
The knife is used with precision to shave off thin layers of wood from the edges of the internal cutout.
The man uses the knife to smooth the inner surfaces of the newly carved hole in the wood.
Hands hold the wooden strip steady while the knife tip is used to clean up the corners of the cutout.
The person shaves the surface of the wood near the cutout to create a tapered or beveled effect.
More wood shavings accumulate on the person's lap as the carving process progresses.
The woodworker uses the knife to deepen the notch being carved into the side of the wooden piece.
The blade is carefully guided to remove a small sliver of wood from the edge of the tool being made.
The man continues to work on the wooden shuttle, using the knife to refine the shape of the central prong.
Close-up of the knife blade slicing through the wood to create a smooth, curved surface.
The person uses the knife to shave the sides of the wooden piece, making it thinner and more uniform.
Hands rotate the wooden piece to access a different angle for further carving with the sharp knife.
The craftsman carefully removes a thin layer of wood from the end of the strip to shape it.
The knife is used to carve a point or taper onto one end of the wooden shuttle.
Detailed carving continues as the man works on the intricate parts of the wooden weaving tool.
The person uses the knife to scrape along the surface of the wood, smoothing out any rough patches.
Small bits of wood are flicked away by the knife as the final shape of the tool begins to emerge.
The man pauses to inspect his work, checking the symmetry and finish of the carved wooden object.
Resuming the work, the craftsman uses the knife to make fine adjustments to the shuttle's shape.
The knife blade is used to carve a small groove or indentation into the wooden surface.
Hands work steadily to refine the details of the wooden tool, removing tiny amounts of material at a time.
The person uses the knife to round off the edges of the wooden strip for a more comfortable grip.
Close-up of the wood being carved, showing the texture of the wood and the sharpness of the blade.
The man continues to carve the central part of the shuttle, making sure it is properly hollowed out.
Using the tip of the knife, the woodworker cleans out the interior of the carved slot.
The knife is used to shave the outer edges of the wooden piece to achieve the desired width.
The craftsman works on the other end of the wooden strip, carving it to match the first end.
Hands move the knife in a controlled manner to create a smooth, continuous curve along the wood.
The woodworker focuses on the fine details, ensuring every part of the shuttle is well-crafted.
A thin sliver of wood is removed from the side of the tool to improve its balance and form.
The person uses the knife to carve a small notch that will hold the thread or twine in place.
Detailed work on the wooden shuttle continues as the man uses the knife to refine its overall appearance.
The craftsman shaves the surface of the wood to remove any remaining knife marks or irregularities.
Hands hold the wooden tool up to the light to check for any imperfections in the carving.
The woodworker uses the knife to make a final few cuts to perfect the shape of the shuttle.
The person uses a piece of sandpaper or a rough cloth to smooth the surface of the carved wood.
The finished wooden shuttle is shown, ready to be used for weaving or netting.
The man sets down the knife and admires the completed wooden tool he has just carved.
